If the behavior continues, **therapy (individual or couples) and safety planning** may be necessary. - **For John:** If he genuinely wants to change, he should: - **Acknowledge the harm** (even if he doesn’t fully understand it). - **Seek therapy** (especially **emotionally focused therapy (EFT)** or **cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)** for abusive patterns). - **Work on empathy** (understanding how his actions affect his partner). ### **When to Seek Help:** If this is part of a **pattern of abuse** (e.g., verbal insults, threats, isolation), the wife should: ✅ **Reach out to a domestic violence hotline** (e.g., [The Hotline](https://www.thehotline.org/) in the U.S.). ✅ **Document incidents** (for safety and legal purposes). ✅ **Consider leaving if she feels unsafe**—abuse is **never the victim’s fault**.
